news.headline: A Super-Sniffer Labrador Is Animal of the Year
news.body: A black Labrador named Sgiath (pronounced "Skee-ah") from the Scottish Highlands was named Animal of the Year by the animal charity IFAW. Sgiath used to help find lost hikers in the mountains, but now she sniffs out a slimy sea creature nicknamed "sea vomit" that harms ocean wildlife. When she finds it, she stands very still and stares instead of barking. She has already found hundreds of patches of the gooey stuff!

news.headline: 15 Teeny-Tiny Froglets Hatch in a World First
news.body: London Zoo welcomed 15 baby Afia Birago's puddle frogs, one of the rarest and smallest frogs on Earth. Each froglet is about as big as the tip of a pencil! It is the first time this kind of frog has ever been born in a zoo. In the wild, they live in just two pools in a forest in Ghana, so keepers are sharing what they learn to help the frogs back home.

news.headline: A Skateboarder Zooms Into the Record Books
news.body: Pro skateboarder Diego Poncelet set a new world record for the fastest standing ride down a hill: about 94 miles per hour! He raced down a long, curvy road in Quebec, Canada, wearing a special suit and riding a board with a smooth shell to slice through the wind. Guinness World Records says he went as fast as hurricane winds. He even beat the old record held by his friend.

fun_fact: Most frogs don't drink water with their mouths. They soak it up through their skin, especially a special patch on their belly! 🐸
